code.driver.database.why: Store, query and traverse a property graph inside its own process without running a database server.
code.driver.database.how: Exposes Database and Connection types that open a database, run Cypher text or prepared statements, and return typed rows.

code.driver.database.why: Place partitions of a partitioned node table on other hosts while the engine stays unaware of distribution.
code.driver.database.how: Exposes RoutingGuard and Callbacks that claim partitions, observe their creation and drop, and receive each row routed to a claimed partition.

code.handle.database.why: Open or create an on-disk or in-memory database with the caller's resource limits.
code.handle.database.how: Database::new and Database::in_memory take a path and a SystemConfig (buffer pool size, thread count, read-only, checkpoint and WAL options) and own the engine instance.

code.connection.database.why: Let callers submit Cypher text and parameters and get results back.
code.connection.database.how: Connection::query runs text, prepare and execute run parameterised statements, and interrupt and set_query_timeout end long queries.

code.result.query.why: Give callers the rows and column metadata an executed query produced.
code.result.query.how: QueryResult iterates rows as Vec<Value>, reports column names, types, tuple counts and timings, and exports Arrow batches or CSR arrays under the arrow feature.

code.converter.value.why: Carry typed data between Rust and the engine in parameters and results.
code.converter.value.how: The Value enum and LogicalType mirror the engine type system (integers, temporal types, lists, structs, nodes, relationships, maps) and convert both ways.

code.router.partition.why: Expose the engine's distributed partition-routing hooks to wrapper authors.
code.router.partition.how: RoutingGuard::install registers process-global Callbacks before any Database opens; the module also keeps a row store and scan for claimed partitions.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Call the C++ engine from safe Rust.
code.bridge.ffi.how: A cxx bridge in ffi.rs declares the engine types and the shim functions in lbug_rs.cpp, and turns C++ exceptions into Error values.

code.script.build.why: Obtain and link a compiled engine at build time.
code.script.build.how: build.rs selects an external library, a downloaded prebuilt static archive, or a source build, then links it and compiles the shim.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Create the engine database instance and hand it to connections.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Calls database_new through the cxx bridge with the path and each SystemConfig field.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Submit query text and parameters to the engine and receive its result object.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Calls connection_query, connection_prepare and connection_execute and reads the success flag and error message into Error::FailedQuery.

code.handle.database.why: Open a connection that stays valid only while its database lives.
code.handle.database.how: Connection::new borrows the Database and takes the engine connection from it.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Read rows, column names and timings from the engine result.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Calls has_next and get_next on the C++ result and reads each flat tuple value.

code.converter.value.why: Turn each engine cell into a Rust value.
code.converter.value.how: Converts every FFI value into a Value with try_into while iterating.

code.converter.value.why: Pass prepared-statement parameters in engine types.
code.converter.value.how: Converts each (name, Value) pair into an FFI value before execute.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Read and build engine values and logical types.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Uses FFI value and logical-type accessors and constructors for each Value variant.

code.bridge.ffi.arrow.why: Register Arrow memory as node or relationship tables and run Arrow-native queries.
code.bridge.ffi.arrow.how: create_arrow_table, create_arrow_rel_table, create_arrow_rel_table_csr, drop_arrow_table and query_as_arrow call the arrow bridge under the arrow feature.

code.bridge.ffi.arrow.why: Hand query results to callers as Arrow record batches and CSR arrays.
code.bridge.ffi.arrow.how: iter_arrow and csr pull chunks and index arrays across the arrow bridge.

upstream.library.arrow.why: Represent exchanged data as Arrow C data interface structures.
upstream.library.arrow.how: Wraps arrow FFI_ArrowArray and FFI_ArrowSchema as cxx external types.

upstream.engine.database.graph.why: Execute Cypher, store and read graph data.
upstream.engine.database.graph.how: The shim lbug_rs.cpp includes the engine header and calls its Database, Connection, PreparedStatement and QueryResult classes.

upstream.engine.database.graph.why: Install process-global hooks and receive routed partition events.
upstream.engine.database.graph.how: A separate C ABI shim (lbug_partition_routing.cpp) registers PartitionRoutingHooks and keeps a row store and scan table function for claimed partitions.

code.converter.value.why: Decode routed rows and describe parent schema columns.
code.converter.value.how: Passes each inserted row to the callback as Vec<Value> and maps LogicalType to engine type ids in register_parent_schema.

upstream.archive.library.how: Runs scripts/download_lbug.sh to fetch a prebuilt static liblbug into .cache, then links it.

upstream.engine.database.graph.why: Compile the engine when no prebuilt archive is available or a source build is requested.
upstream.engine.database.graph.how: Builds lbug-src (or LBUG_SOURCE_DIR) with CMake and links the result statically.

code.result.query.why: Give callers the rows and column metadata an executed query produced.
code.result.query.how: QueryResult iterates rows as Vec<Value>, reports column names, types, tuple counts and timings, prints as text, and exports Arrow batches or CSR arrays under the arrow feature. The exported CSVOptions type is not used by any function in this crate.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Call the C++ engine from safe Rust and report failures.
code.bridge.ffi.how: A cxx bridge in ffi.rs declares the engine types and the shim functions in lbug_rs.cpp. The Error enum (error.rs) carries failed query, failed prepare, C++ exception, read-only type and JSON failures to callers.
